newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X, SNC-Lavalin targets of Canada suit.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X, SNC-Lavalin targets of Canada suit.

text.p: Canadian lawyers said on Thursday they had filed a class action lawsuit in a Canadian court against gold prospector Bre-X Minerals Ltd and engineering firm SNC-Lavalin Group Inc.
The lawsuit was filed earlier today in a court in Windsor, Ontario, by law firm Gignac, Sutts said in a statement.
This is the first class action suit launched against the Calgary-based exploration company in Canada. Bre-X is currently facing at least five lawsuits in the United States.
Gignac, Sutts said it is seeking unspecified "damages arising out of the recent collapse in the price of the common shares of Bre-X Minerals Ltd."
Panic selling lopped nearly C$3 billion off of Bre-X's stock market value last Thursday amid doubts over the size and viability of the company's Busang gold deposit in Indonesia.
Trading in Bre-X shares was stopped on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday, the third time this week the TSE has halted trading in the volatile stock.
The stock last traded up 0.23 at 3.43 on volume of 5.02 million shares on Thursday. Heavy order volumes and technical problems have overwhelmed the TSE's 20-year-old trading system.

SNC-Lavalin Group Inc was also named in the Canadian court action. SNC-Lavalin's subsidiary, Kilborn SNC-Lavalin Inc, performed the resource calculations on Busang for Bre-X, which has claimed the site contains 70.95 million ounces of gold.
Earlier on Thursday, the Toronto Stock Exchange and Ontario Securities Commission released a detailed report by Kilborn on Bre-X's assay methods.
However, the TSE and securities regulator said Bre-X has stated that the report contains no new material information.
